- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 5–10 days.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior 5-day avg), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +5% above recent peak for 3–7 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to avoid premature mean reversion.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >3% from 14-day moving average, adjust forecast toward historical mean of last 18 days.
- When sentiment flips from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift to capture momentum.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating 0.33/1.00), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast using 5-day weighted average for next 7 days.
